Else ... thou--</hi>He changes from the first person, as he had just expressed his own resolution, "I will pray with the understanding," whatever "thou" doest.<div eID="gen33787" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33788" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bless--</hi>the highest kind of prayer.<div eID="gen33788" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33789" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">occupieth the room of the unlearned--</hi>one who, whatever other gifts he may possess, yet, as wanting the gift of interpretation, is reduced by the speaking in an unknown tongue to the position of one unlearned, or "a private person."<div eID="gen33789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33790" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">say Amen--</hi>Prayer is not a vicarious duty done by others for us; as in Rome's liturgies and masses. The followers of Apollos prided themselves as "spiritual" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.1-1Cor.3.3">1Co 3:1-3</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Gal.6.1">Ga 6:1</reference>). Here one capable of discerning spirits is specially meant.<div eID="gen33836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33837" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">things that I write ... commandments of the Lord--</hi>a direct assertion of inspiration. Paul's words as an apostle are Christ's words. Paul appeals not merely to one or two, but to a body of men, for the reality of three facts about which no body of men could possibly be mistaken: (1) that his having converted them was not due to mere eloquence, but to the "demonstration of the Spirit and of power"; (2) that part of this demonstration consisted in the communication of miraculous power, which they were then exercising so generally as to require to be corrected in the irregular employment of it; (3) that among these miraculous gifts was one which enabled the "prophet" or "spiritual person" to decide whether Paul's Epistle was Scripture or not.
